findings.quote: confirming that EY had concluded their work in relation to four objections from a local elector on the 2023/24 financial statements

findings.paper_title: Statement of Accounts 2023/24
findings.headline: Auditors requested an additional disclosure acknowledging 'the challenging landscape' facing Cheshire East and other local authorities.
findings.detail: EY required the council to add explicit disclosure language about difficult financial circumstances in the final accounts. This is a step beyond normal reporting and signals auditor concern about the broader financial position.
findings.matters: Required disclosures of financial difficulty are red flags for lenders and indicate auditor concern about going concern or sustainability of council operations.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: EY had requested that an additional disclosure was included in the final version of the SoA in recognition of the challenging landscape within which Cheshire East Council and other local authorities find themselves.

findings.paper_title: Statement of Accounts 2023/24
findings.headline: The council is under financial pressure and must 'learn to live within our means', suggesting structural deficit or spending control issues.
findings.detail: The report explicitly identifies that the committee needs to scrutinise 'the financial pressure the Council is facing' and identify actions to 'learn to live within our means'. This language indicates the council is spending more than it can afford and requires corrective action.
findings.matters: Councils unable to live within their means face escalating deficits, reserve depletion, and potential need for emergency borrowing or government intervention—all material risks to lenders.
findings.figures: No specific deficit figures disclosed in this summary document; full detail expected in Audit Completion Report.
findings.quote: This report is important to ensure Members of the Committee are sighted on the financial pressure the Council is facing and the activity to date to try and mitigate this issue, and are given an opportunity to scrutinise this activity and identify any further actions that could be taken to learn to live within our means

findings.paper_title: Statement of Accounts 2023/24
findings.headline: Auditors issued a disclaimed opinion because they could not obtain sufficient evidence to conclude the accounts are free from material misstatement.
findings.detail: Ernst & Young could not gather enough evidence before the statutory deadline to give an opinion on whether Cheshire East's 2023/24 financial statements are accurate. A disclaimed opinion means the auditors are unable to verify the accounts' reliability. This represents a material audit failure and goes beyond qualified opinions.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion signals that financial statements cannot be verified as accurate—a critical concern for lenders assessing creditworthiness and for finance directors who need reliable accounts for decision-making.
findings.figures: Backstop date for audit: 28/02/2025; audit conducted after this date without issuing full opinion
findings.quote: EY were not in a position to obtain sufficient evidence to be able to conclude that the financial statements of the Council are free from material and pervasive misstatement before the backstop date for the 2023/24 accounts (28/02/2025) and therefore anticipate issuing a disclaimed 2023/24 audit opinion.

findings.paper_title: Officer Decision Records - Internal Audit Briefing
findings.headline: Decisions made without appropriate delegated authority due to outdated schemes of delegation
findings.detail: Testing identified decisions made by officers without appropriate delegated authority, where schemes of delegation were not up to date and it was not therefore possible to confirm that appropriate delegations were in place. Internal audit found no evidence that any decisions were inappropriate or that officers deliberately bypassed due process.
findings.matters: Lack of proper delegated authority is a control environment risk, though the absence of substantive impropriety suggests this was primarily a documentation and clarity issue rather than a deliberate circumvention.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Testing identified decisions that had been made without the appropriate delegated authority. This included instances where decisions were made by officers without the appropriate level of delegated authority, or where schemes of delegation were not up to date

findings.paper_title: Officer Decision Records - Internal Audit Briefing
findings.headline: Instances of delayed or unpublished Officer Decision Records creating transparency and compliance breaches
findings.detail: Testing found delays in publication of ODRs and instances where ODRs were not published at all. This created risk of decisions not being subject to appropriate transparency and challenge, along with potential breaches of the Openness Regulations 2014 and the Council's Constitution.
findings.matters: Failure to comply with Openness Regulations may constitute breach of statutory duty and expose the council to legal challenge and reputational damage.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Testing identified instances where there had been delays in the publication of ODR's and some instances where ODR's had not been published at all.

findings.paper_title: Officer Decision Records - Internal Audit Briefing
findings.headline: Officer Decision Records process received Limited Assurance opinion, indicating control environment weaknesses
findings.detail: Internal audit review found inconsistencies in understanding and application of ODR processes across departments, posing risks to governance and transparency. The review identified risks that decisions may not have been subject to required transparency and scrutiny, and may not comply with the Openness Regulations and the Council's Constitution. The council is implementing remediation including a new single form, centralized tracking via modern.gov, and detailed training, with the new process going live in January 2026.
findings.matters: Limited Assurance on a core governance process indicates control environment weaknesses that lenders view as a risk factor for the quality of council decision-making and operations.
findings.figures: During 2022/23 and 2023/24 a total of 147 decisions were published, of which 41 were identified as 'significant'; 44 ODRs published prior to December 2024, with a further 24 up to the end of the financial year
findings.quote: The review identified inconsistencies in the understanding and application of ODR processes, posing risks to governance and transparency. A "Limited Assurance" opinion was provided

findings.paper_title: Audit and Governance Committee Action Log
findings.headline: Planning Department governance and internal control concerns flagged by committee
findings.detail: The Audit and Governance Committee was asked to investigate ongoing planning website issues that generated resident criticism. The request specifically raised concerns about whether governance arrangements and internal controls are in place and working effectively.
findings.matters: Planning website failures indicate operational control weaknesses; committee's investigation suggests audit concern about the robustness of governance arrangements.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: Concerns were raised in relation to the ongoing issues with the planning website which had resulted in criticism from residents. It was requested that the committee considered looking into this matter to ensure the governance arrangements and internal controls were in place and working.

findings.paper_title: Audit and Governance Committee Action Log
findings.headline: External auditors required going concern disclosure in 2023-24 accounts due to challenging financial landscape
findings.detail: The council's 2023/24 Annual Governance Statement was amended to include an additional disclosure on going concern after external auditors specifically requested it. The auditors cited the 'challenging landscape' facing Cheshire East Council and other local authorities as the reason for requiring this disclosure.
findings.matters: Going concern disclosures signal auditor doubts about an entity's ability to continue operating; this is a critical risk indicator for lenders assessing council creditworthiness.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: In finalising their audit work on the 2023/24 statement of accounts, the external auditors requested that the Council include an additional disclosure on going concern in recognition of the challenging landscape within which Cheshire East Council and other local authorities find themselves.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts 2023/24 , item 46.
findings.headline: Council's strategic risk register contains multiple critically-rated risks that have persisted for extended periods.
findings.detail: The audit report notes that 'The Council's Strategic Risk Register contains a number of critically rated risks which have been present for considerable periods of time'. Combined with identified gaps in partnership working governance and poor cross-service relationships, the council has not maintained an effective control environment.
findings.matters: Long-standing critical risks that remain unresolved suggest weak risk management, failure of leadership accountability, and capacity constraints that could materialise into operational failures.
findings.figures: Multiple critical risks; described as 'present for considerable periods of time'
findings.quote: The Council's Strategic Risk Register contains a number of critically rated risks which have been present for considerable periods of time

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts 2023/24 , item 46.
findings.headline: 38% of internal audit actions in 2023/24 related to failure to apply existing controls; council awarded No Assurance opinion on Section 106 arrangements.
findings.detail: Of 184 internal audit actions raised during the year, 38% related to a failure to apply existing controls and 13% identified an absence of an expected or actual control. The Council received a 'No Assurance' opinion from internal audit on Section 106 arrangements. Internal Audit issued a 'limited assurance' opinion for 2023/24, and the Council identified in the Annual Governance Statement areas where improvements in control are required.
findings.matters: Systemic failure to apply known controls indicates weak internal governance and risk that funds are not being appropriately managed; Section 106 'No Assurance' rating poses compliance and financial risk.
findings.figures: 38% of 184 actions = failure to apply controls; 13% = absence of controls; Section 106 No Assurance opinion
findings.quote: of 184 actions raised, 38% related to a failure to apply existing controls, with a further 13% identifying an absence of an expected or actual control. In the year, there was an opinion of 'No Assurance' awarded in relation to Section 106 arrangements

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts 2023/24 , item 46.
findings.headline: Ofsted rated Children's Social Care Services inadequate; Secretary of State issued improvement notice requiring external improvement advisor.
findings.detail: The 2024 Ofsted inspection report rated the Council's children's services as inadequate, calling for stronger senior leader oversight, better support for care leavers, improved management supervision, more effective child-focused planning, consistent visits, increased placement availability, and greater impact from child protection chairs. On 24 July 2024, the Secretary of State issued an improvement notice requiring the Council to cooperate with an independent improvement advisor appointed to deliver improvements.
findings.matters: A statutory improvement notice for children's services indicates serious safeguarding concerns and operational failure; it constrains the council's autonomy and signals reputational and legal risk.
findings.figures: Inspection 16 May 2024; improvement notice 24 July 2024; Ofsted rating: inadequate
findings.quote: The 2024 Ofsted report rated the Council's children's services as inadequate...On 24 July 2024, the Secretary of State issued an improvement notice to the Council after Ofsted's 16 May 2024 inspection report raised significant concerns about Children's Social Care Services

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts 2023/24 , item 46.
findings.headline: Council received Exceptional Financial Support and Best Value Notice due to financial sustainability concerns.
findings.detail: On 20 February 2025, the Government named Cheshire East among 30 councils receiving Exceptional Financial Support, providing £17.6m for 2024/25 and £25.3m for 2025/26 — both 'expected to be fully utilised'. On 8 May 2025, the Council received a Best Value Notice from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government. Key reports including LGA peer challenge and CIPFA review highlighted issues with leadership capacity, governance, scrutiny, and organisational culture.
findings.matters: Central government intervention through Exceptional Financial Support and Best Value Notice signals fundamental concerns about the council's financial health and governance; both are reserved for councils in crisis.
findings.figures: £17.6m EFS 2024/25; £25.3m EFS 2025/26; issued 20 February 2025; Best Value Notice issued 8 May 2025
findings.quote: On 20 February 2025, the Government named the Council among 30 councils receiving Exceptional Financial Support, agreeing in-principle to £17.6m for 2024/25 and £25.3m for 2025/26, both expected to be fully utilised...On 8 May 2025, the Council received a Best Value Notice from the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government due to financial sustainability concerns

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts 2023/24 , item 46.
findings.headline: Council overspent revenue budget by £8.5m in 2023/24 and depleted General Fund reserves by 47% in a single year, with 70% of remaining reserves committed to cover 2024/25 overspend.
findings.detail: General Fund Balances fell from £81.1m (31 March 2023) to £43.2m (31 March 2024). Section 151 officer stated in February 2024 that 'ongoing reliance on reserves was not sustainable'. In February 2025, the Interim Executive Director warned that a forecasted 2024/25 overspend of £18.3m means 'current reserve levels are insufficient to cover the projected revenue outturn without further measures'. More than £22m (70.5%) of total earmarked reserves is allocated to support 2024/25 budget.
findings.matters: Rapid reserve depletion and structural overspending indicates the council is not living within its means and is using non-renewable resources to mask a deficit spending problem.
findings.figures: £81.1m (31 Mar 2023) to £43.2m (31 Mar 2024); £8.5m overspend 2023/24; £18.3m forecast overspend 2024/25; £22m (70.5% of reserves) committed to 2024/25
findings.quote: To achieve this position the Council reduced its General Fund Balances from £81.1m at 31 March 2023...to £43.2m at 31 March 2024...ongoing reliance on reserves was not sustainable in the medium term

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts 2023/24 , item 46.
findings.headline: Auditor has disclaimed the 2023/24 audit opinion — unable to conclude whether financial statements are free from material misstatement.
findings.detail: Ernst & Young could not complete necessary audit procedures and obtain sufficient audit evidence due to late appointment, the 2022/23 audit not being concluded, and delays in receiving evidence. The auditor did not issue an unmodified opinion and cannot provide reasonable assurance on the financial statements.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion means financial statements lack independent verification, creating uncertainty for lenders about the council's true financial position and control environment.
findings.figures: No opinion issued; backstop date of 28 February 2025 missed; report issued 28 November 2025
findings.quote: Due to the delay in completing the prior year audit, our late appointment as auditors of the Council for the financial year ending 31 March 2024 and delays in receiving evidence we were not in a position to complete the detailed audit procedures that would be needed to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to issue an unmodified audit report

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Internal Audit Plan Update , item 48.
findings.headline: Five audit action recommendations remain overdue for implementation as of end September 2025
findings.detail: Of 42 outstanding audit actions from previous audits, 5 were overdue at 30 September 2025 (12 per cent overdue rate). These have been raised with Executive Directors, indicating control improvement recommendations have not been implemented within agreed timescales.
findings.matters: Overdue implementation of audit recommendations means identified control weaknesses remain unaddressed, prolonging the council's exposure to the risks those controls are designed to mitigate.
findings.figures: 5 overdue actions out of 42 total outstanding (12% overdue)
findings.quote: The table above demonstrates that at the end of September 2025 only 12% of outstanding actions were overdue for implementation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Internal Audit Plan Update , item 48.
findings.headline: Council received 'limited' audit opinion on control framework for 2024/25
findings.detail: The Head of Audit Risk and Assurance gave a 'limited' opinion on the Council's governance, risk management and internal control for 2024/25. This indicates material weaknesses in the control environment, though the report notes a positive direction of travel year on year.
findings.matters: A limited audit opinion from internal audit indicates governance and control weaknesses that could affect financial management, compliance and risk management effectiveness.
findings.figures: Opinion rated as 'limited' for 2024/25
findings.quote: the Head of Audit Risk and Assurance's opinion as the Chief Audit Executive on the Council's framework for governance, risk management and internal control for 2024/25 was given as "limited".

findings.paper_title: Provisional Audit Planning Report (Update) of Ernst & Young LLP - 2024/25
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127420/Provisional Audit Planning Report Update of Ernst Young LLP - 202425 Decision Report Template .pdf
findings.headline: Risk that audit testing will not be completed by the 27 February 2026 statutory deadline
findings.detail: The audit timeline has shifted from September-November to November-February testing, with a pause between 12 December 2025 and 5 January 2026. The report explicitly states there is a potential risk that not all testing work will be completed in this compressed timeframe before the statutory backstop date of 27 February 2026.
findings.matters: If audit work cannot be completed by the backstop date, the auditor will be forced to issue a disclaimed opinion by default, further damaging the council's financial credibility and access to credit markets.
findings.figures: 27 February 2026 backstop date; testing window 12 December 2025 to 5 January 2026 pause
findings.quote: Due to the change in the testing period there is a potential risk that not all of the testing work will be completed in the timeframe.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Audit Planning Report (Update) of Ernst & Young LLP - 2024/25
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127420/Provisional Audit Planning Report Update of Ernst Young LLP - 202425 Decision Report Template .pdf
findings.headline: 2024/25 audit expected to produce another disclaimed opinion due to unresolved issues cascading from the prior year
findings.detail: Because EY could not gain assurance over closing balances in 2023/24, they have no assurance over opening balances for 2024/25. This means they cannot obtain assurance over in-year movements and some closing balances for 2024/25, leading EY to indicate they expect to issue a disclaimed audit opinion again for 2024/25.
findings.matters: Two consecutive disclaimed audit opinions indicate systemic failures in the council's financial controls and record-keeping that persist across multiple years, suggesting deep structural problems rather than isolated issues.
findings.quote: Having not gained assurance over the closing balances in 2023/24, EY report that they do not have assurance over the opening balances for 2024/25. Hence, this means EY do not have assurance over in-year movements and some closing balances for 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Provisional Audit Planning Report (Update) of Ernst & Young LLP - 2024/25
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127420/Provisional Audit Planning Report Update of Ernst Young LLP - 202425 Decision Report Template .pdf
findings.headline: Auditor will disclaim opinion on 2023/24 financial statements, indicating inability to form a reliable audit conclusion
findings.detail: Ernst & Young have reported that they anticipate issuing a disclaimed audit opinion on the 2023/24 financial statements. A disclaimed opinion is the most serious audit outcome, meaning the auditor was unable to gather sufficient evidence to form an opinion on whether the accounts present a true and fair view.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion signals fundamental problems with the council's financial records, documentation, or controls, which directly impacts the reliability of financial reporting that lenders use to assess creditworthiness and financial stability.
findings.figures: 2023/24 financial year
findings.quote: EY anticipate issuing a disclaimed audit opinion on the Council's 2023/24 financial statements.

findings.paper_title: Final Statement of Accounts 2023-24 (report to follow)
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127633/Statement of Accounts Update 2324 Decision Report Template delete as appropriate.pdf
findings.headline: The council missed the 28/02/2025 statutory backstop date for finalizing the 2023/24 accounts.
findings.detail: The council did not meet the required deadline for completion and publication of the 2023/24 Statement of Accounts. The then S151 Officer was required to publish an explanation on the council's website. As of this September 2025 report, the accounts remain unfinal and awaiting the completed audit report.
findings.matters: Missing statutory deadlines for account finalization signals governance or operational capacity issues and delays stakeholder access to financial information.
findings.figures: Missed deadline: 28/02/2025; Report date: 29/09/2025 (seven months late)
findings.quote: As the 28/02/2025 backstop date for the 2023/24 wasn't met, the then Interim Executive Director of Resources (S151), Adele Taylor, published an explanation on the Council's website.

findings.paper_title: Final Statement of Accounts 2023-24 (report to follow)
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127633/Statement of Accounts Update 2324 Decision Report Template delete as appropriate.pdf
findings.headline: The disclaimed audit opinion is expected to persist for several years, preventing recovery to an unmodified opinion in the near term.
findings.detail: Following a disclaimed opinion, auditors in subsequent years will lack assurance over opening balances and comparative figures carried forward from the prior year. This creates a cascading effect where the disclaimed opinion in 2023/24 is likely to result in disclaimed opinions for multiple years before the council can recover to an unmodified opinion.
findings.matters: Years of consecutive disclaimed opinions prevent lenders from obtaining reliable multi-year financial trends and signal ongoing systemic issues.
findings.figures: Expected duration: several years before recovery to unmodified opinion
findings.quote: It is likely therefore that a disclaimed audit in year 2023/24 may not recover for a number of years to an unmodified opinion.

findings.paper_title: Final Statement of Accounts 2023-24 (report to follow)
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127633/Statement of Accounts Update 2324 Decision Report Template delete as appropriate.pdf
findings.headline: Four objections from a local elector on the 2023/24 financial statements were accepted by auditors and required investigation.
findings.detail: EY accepted four formal objections from a member of the public to the 2023/24 financial statements. These objections required substantial audit investigation before the auditors could proceed with their opinion. The delay caused by these objections prevented the auditors from finalizing their opinion by the statutory deadline.
findings.matters: Contested financial statements suggest potential issues in accounting practices or financial reporting; public objections indicate stakeholder concerns about reliability.
findings.figures: Number of objections accepted: 4
findings.quote: Ernst & Young LLP (EY) had accepted four objections from a local elector on the 2023/24 financial statements and until these objections have been considered, EY would not be in a position to issue their proposed disclaimed audit opinion.

findings.paper_title: Final Statement of Accounts 2023-24 (report to follow)
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127633/Statement of Accounts Update 2324 Decision Report Template delete as appropriate.pdf
findings.headline: Council's auditors have requested a going concern disclosure due to the council's financial position and challenging financial landscape.
findings.detail: EY required the council to add a going concern disclosure covering up to 12 months from account authorization. This was requested based on recognition of the council's own financial position and the challenging landscape facing local authorities. The council's financial performance since 2022 was flagged as a going concern risk in EY's audit plan.
findings.matters: Going concern disclosures signal potential inability to continue operations; lenders view this as a material indicator of financial distress requiring close monitoring.
findings.figures: Assessment period: up to 12 months from date of authorization
findings.quote: A going concern assessment is deemed necessary in recognition of the Councils financial position and also the ongoing challenging landscape within which Cheshire East Council and other local authorities find themselves. findings.paper_title: Final Statement of Accounts 2023-24 (report to follow)
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127633/Statement of Accounts Update 2324 Decision Report Template delete as appropriate.pdf

findings.paper_title: Final Annual Governance Statement 2023-24
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127491/Final Annual Governance Statement 202324 Decision Report Template delete as appropriate.pdf

findings.paper_title: Audit and Governance Committee Action Log
findings.headline: The committee identified variances in wholly owned companies' 2024-25 financial statements and required management responses.
findings.detail: The committee noted variances in draft financial statements and outturn for wholly owned companies and sought explicit assurance from management about steps being taken to address them. Officers committed to obtain responses from the WOCs, which have been circulated to the committee.
findings.matters: Unexplained variances in owned-company accounts can indicate financial control weaknesses or hidden liabilities affecting the council's overall financial position.
findings.quote: The committee sought assurance relating to the steps being taken by management (Wholly Owned Companies) in relation to variances identified in the draft financial statements 2024-25 and outturn update 2024-25.

findings.paper_title: Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/b28911/Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda 29th-Sep-2025 10.30 Audit and Governance Committ.pdf?T=9
findings.headline: Section 114 (financial failure) is now a realistic risk if in-year spending drifts
findings.detail: The going concern statement explicitly notes that the reserve position is 'clearly unsustainable' and that 'a 1% variance in spending could trigger the requirement for a Section 114 report'. Section 114 is the statutory mechanism by which a council declares it cannot balance its budget and is effectively bankrupt.
findings.matters: A Section 114 notice is a formal declaration of financial failure. The fact that a 1% variance could trigger it shows the council has zero margin for error.
findings.figures: General reserves at £5.6m against a net revenue budget of £353.1m for 2023/24
findings.quote: This position being clearly unsustainable as a 1% variance in spending could trigger the requirement for a Section 114 report.

findings.paper_title: Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/b28911/Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda 29th-Sep-2025 10.30 Audit and Governance Committ.pdf?T=9
findings.headline: HS2 cancellation imposes £8.7m unbudgeted cost charged to revenue and reserves
findings.detail: The government's cancellation of HS2 Phase 2 meant costs the council expected to recover from project funding were instead charged to reserves as revenue spend. The council had to treat £8.7m of HS2 costs as revenue expenditure with no prospect of future income to offset it.
findings.matters: An unbudgeted £8.7m charge to reserves from a government policy decision illustrates the council's exposure to policy risks outside its control and the cost of prior strategic investments that no longer exist.
findings.figures: £8.7m of HS2 spending charged to reserves as revenue
findings.quote: The Government's decision to cancel HS2 Phase 2 also meant that costs associated with that project, that were expected to be funded from future income, were expected to be funded from existing reserves, with no prospect of future income.

findings.paper_title: Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/b28911/Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda 29th-Sep-2025 10.30 Audit and Governance Committ.pdf?T=9
findings.headline: Large debt (£284m) in high interest rate environment; capital programme deferred to ease financing pressure
findings.detail: The council holds £284m in accumulated debt from large-scale infrastructure projects, past overspends, and DSG deficits. Interest on this debt has become 'a material problem' following rapid rises in rates in 2022–23. The council is deferring capital spending to reduce borrowing needs: forecast capital spend fell from £171.1m (Third Financial Review) to £136.9m (actual outturn). The going concern statement notes the council must 'avoid the risk of over-borrowing'.
findings.matters: High debt in a rising-rate environment increases financing costs and crowds out discretionary spending. The council is rationing capital investment to manage debt service, indicating financial constraint.
findings.figures: Accumulated debt £284m; capital forecast £171.1m vs actual outturn £136.9m (£34.2m slippage); £9.5m of 2024/25 budget growth was for MRP and interest
findings.quote: Interest Rates: In 2023/24 the Council had debts of £284m accumulated from the spending profile of large-scale infrastructure projects, overspending of budgets and the increasing deficit in high needs (SEND) education expenditure. Repayment of interest on these debts became a material problem following the rapid rise in interest rates in 2022 and 2023.

findings.paper_title: Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/b28911/Audit and Govenance Committee - Supplement Agenda 29th-Sep-2025 10.30 Audit and Governance Committ.pdf?T=9
findings.headline: Structural budget gaps of £25.3m (2025/26) and £21.6m (2026/27) forecast even after savings proposals
findings.detail: After identifying £70m of new pressures in 2025/26 and proposing £53m of savings and income, the council still faces a £25.3m gap. For 2026/27, the gap is £21.6m. These gaps are being filled with EFS and reserve drawdowns, not structural solutions. The council must 'learn to live within its means by delivering all savings and containing approved growth' or gaps will widen further.
findings.matters: A £25m+ annual gap that cannot be closed through the normal savings process indicates the council's cost base is structurally misaligned to funding. Filling gaps with reserves or emergency grants is not sustainable.
findings.figures: 2025/26 gap: £25.3m (after £70m of pressures identified and £53m of savings proposed); 2026/27 gap: £21.6m
findings.quote: there remained a reduced £25.3m gap for 2025/26... The budget gap for 2026/27 as per the Feb25 MTFS is £21.6m and is being reviewed alongside in year reporting 2025/26

findings.headline: Council dependent on emergency government grants (EFS) to balance budget; applied full £17.6m in 2024/25
findings.detail: The council received provisional approval for Exceptional Financial Support from central government totalling £17.6m to cover 2023/24 and 2024/25. The 2024/25 outturn overspend of £17.6m was funded entirely by this emergency grant. The council has also applied for and provisionally received EFS for 2025/26. The accounts state the council will 'continue to be reliant on either further EFS or a significant improvement in the level of grant from central government in order to balance future budgets'.
findings.matters: EFS is a bailout from the government, granted on a year-by-year basis and contingent on the council meeting reform conditions. It is not sustainable revenue funding. A lender cannot rely on repeated government grants as a permanent solution.
findings.figures: EFS 2023/24 and 2024/25: £17.6m; EFS 2025/26 provisionally agreed (amount not stated); 2024/25 outturn overspend £17.6m
findings.quote: In February 2024, DLUHC provisionally agreed EFS for 2023/24 and 2024/25 totalling £17.6m... the Council will continue to be reliant on either further EFS or a significant improvement in the level of grant from central government in order to balance future budgets over the medium term.

findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit ballooned to £112m by March 2025, with statutory override masking true liability
findings.detail: The DSG deficit (high needs education spending exceeding grant funding) accumulated to £78.6m by March 2024 and £112m by March 2025. A statutory accounting override allows the council not to cover this from the general fund until 31 March 2028. This masks the true scale of the liability and represents structural overspending in a ring-fenced service that has grown unchecked for years. The council identifies this as 'the single greatest financial risk'.
findings.matters: A £112m hidden deficit represents a massive future liability. When the override expires in 2028, the council will need to find this money from general funds or secure further government relief. This is why it is flagged as the single greatest risk.
findings.figures: DSG deficit £78.6m at 31 March 2024; £112m at 31 March 2025; override extended to 31 March 2028; 2024/25 in-year deficit was £51.3m
findings.quote: The single greatest financial risk to the Council remains the substantial and growing deficit on High Needs spending from the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG)... The accumulated deficit as at 31 March 2024 being £78.6m... The actual deficit at 31 March 2025 being £112m.

findings.headline: General reserves depleted to £5.6m, far below the £20m target
findings.detail: The 2023/24 overspend reduced general reserves from £14.1m to £5.6m. The council's target is £20m (5% of net revenue budget); its benchmark standard is also 5%. At £5.6m, reserves are at only 1.6% of net revenue budget, leaving the council with almost no buffer for adverse variances. The council explicitly states this must be addressed within 12 months.
findings.matters: Reserves are a buffer against unexpected pressures. At 1.6%, the council has minimal financial resilience. The council itself acknowledges that even a 1% variance in spending could trigger a Section 114 notice (statutory financial failure).
findings.figures: General reserves: £5.6m (1.6% of net budget); target £20m (5%); 2023/24 net revenue budget £353.1m
findings.quote: In 2023/24 the £8.5m deficit reduced General Reserves to £5.6m at out-turn... The issue of having low levels of reserves must be addressed within the next 12 months.

findings.headline: 2023/24 overspend of £8.5m filled by drawing down reserves
findings.detail: Despite a £25.4m increase to the net budget for 2023/24, the council overspent by £8.5m, funded entirely from reserves. This follows a £6m overspend in 2022/23, showing a pattern of budget control failure.
findings.matters: Repeated overspends erode reserves and indicate the council cannot manage within approved budgets. This is a sign of control weakness and reduces financial flexibility.
findings.figures: £8.5m overspend in 2023/24; £6m overspend in 2022/23; budget growth of £25.4m
findings.quote: In 2023/24 the increase in net budget was £25.4m, with an out-turn overspend of £8.5m, funded from reserves.

findings.headline: Auditors require going concern disclosure citing the council's challenging financial landscape
findings.detail: EY requested the council add a going concern statement to the accounts despite the Code not normally requiring one, citing the council's financial position and the challenging landscape for local authorities. The disclosure itself runs to several pages detailing cash flow forecasting, medium-term deficits, and reliance on government support, indicating auditor concern about the council's ability to continue.
findings.matters: A going concern disclosure is a red flag. It signals the auditor has doubts about the council's financial viability over the next 12 months and wants those doubts formally disclosed to readers of the accounts.
findings.figures: Council forecasts deficits of £25.3m in 2025/26 and £21.6m in 2026/27; accumulated DSG deficit of £112m by March 2025
findings.quote: EY have requested that the Council include an additional disclosure on going concern in the final 2023/24 version of the SoA in recognition of the challenging landscape within which Cheshire East Council and other local authorities find themselves.

findings.headline: Auditors unable to give full assurance: disclaimed opinion on 2023/24 accounts
findings.detail: Ernst & Young could not obtain sufficient evidence to reach a full audit opinion by the backstop date (28 February 2025) due to pending objections from a local elector. The disclaimed opinion means auditors cannot provide substantive assurance on parts of the financial statements. This will have knock-on effects: in the following year (2024/25), auditors will not have assurance over opening balances from 2023/24, likely perpetuating a disclaimed opinion for several years.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion signals material uncertainty about the accounts and weakens credibility of financial reporting. Lenders rely on auditor assurance; repeated disclaimers suggest underlying problems that are hard to verify or resolve.
findings.figures: Four objections from a local elector accepted by EY; backstop date 28/02/2025 missed
findings.quote: A disclaimed opinion means that the auditor is unable to provide substantive assurance on parts of the financial statements.

findings.headline: PFI liability of £33m being remeasured under new IFRS 16 accounting with implementation uncertainty
findings.detail: The Council has a joint PFI arrangement for Extra Care Housing with a 2023/24 year-end liability of £33m. EY notes the Council had made "little progress" in gathering lease data needed for IFRS 16 implementation as of prior year work. PFI accounting is complex and small errors can be material.
findings.matters: Unresolved IFRS 16 transition issues on a £33m PFI liability could result in material restatement after audit. Implementation delays are a warning sign.
findings.figures: £33m PFI liability as at 31 March 2024
findings.quote: Based on our prior year work the Council had made little progress in collecting the information necessary to implement IFRS 16

findings.headline: Internal Audit opinion on governance and risk management is 'Limited' (weakest rating)
findings.detail: For 2023/24, Internal Audit rated the Council's overall framework as "Limited" on risk management and governance. This is the lowest assurance rating and indicates systemic control weaknesses.
findings.matters: Internal controls that don't work mean the council cannot rely on its own systems to prevent error, fraud, or waste.
findings.figures: Not specified
findings.quote: For 2023/24 Internal Audit (IA) concluded that the overall opinion on the Council's framework of risk management, governance and internal control was "Limited"

findings.headline: LGA peer review concluded financial sustainability is in jeopardy
findings.detail: An independent Local Government Association peer challenge in March 2024 identified that the Council must address significant issues, naming financial sustainability as "in jeopardy" as the most immediate priority. The Council has created a 73-action improvement plan.
findings.matters: An external peer review is an independent verdict on whether the council is being well-run. Calling financial sustainability "in jeopardy" is a stark assessment.
findings.figures: 73 actions across 6 areas
findings.quote: The report identified that the Council needs to address a number of significant issues, the most immediate being the organisation's financial sustainability which is in jeopardy.

findings.headline: OFSTED failure in Children's Services triggered Secretary of State improvement notice (24 July 2024)
findings.detail: OFSTED inspected the Council's Children's Social Care and found significant concerns. The Secretary of State issued a formal improvement notice and retained an Improvement Adviser. The Council must deliver a recovery plan. This is governance failure on a statutory service.
findings.matters: Statutory services failure attracts minister-level intervention, reputational damage, and regulatory risk. It can restrict borrowing and affect grant funding.
findings.figures: Improvement notice issued 24 July 2024; OFSTED report 16 May 2024
findings.quote: On the 24 July 2024 the Secretary of State issued an improvement notice to the Council following the significant concerns highlighted by the publication of OFSTED's inspection report of the Council's Children's Social Care Services on 16 May 2024.

findings.headline: Council already negotiating Exception Financial Support (bailout) funding with MHCLG
findings.detail: The Council is in active liaison with the Ministry for Housing, Communities and Local Government to access Exception Financial Support, a last-resort government bailout. This is conditional on the Council maintaining an approved transformation plan.
findings.matters: The Council is already in de facto insolvency talks with central government. Continued funding is conditional and political.
findings.figures: Not specified
findings.quote: The Council has been in regular liaison with MHCLG to ensure that there is access to Exception Financial Support (EFS) when required, fulfilling the conditions directed by the Minister to have in-place, a transformation plan.

findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127421/Appendix A for Provisional Audit Planning Report Update of Ernst Young LLP - 202425.pdf
findings.headline: Council at material risk of issuing S114 notice (formal insolvency declaration)
findings.detail: EY identifies the Medium Term Financial Strategy as unsustainable without central government support, and flags an explicit risk that the Council will issue a S114 notice (the statutory declaration that a council cannot set a balanced budget and is effectively insolvent).
findings.matters: S114 is a serious statutory intervention threshold. It signals the council cannot fund services from its own resources and requires government rescue.
findings.figures: Not specified
findings.quote: The Council's Medium Term Financial Strategy is not sustainable without central Government support and the Council is at risk of issuing a S114 notice in the future.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Provisional Audit Planning Report (Update) of Ernst & Young LLP - 2024/25 , item 35.
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127421/Appendix A for Provisional Audit Planning Report Update of Ernst Young LLP - 202425.pdf
findings.headline: General Fund reserves depleted by £37.9m in one year; Council at risk of going concern qualification
findings.detail: General Fund balances fell from £81.1m (31 March 2023) to £43.2m (31 March 2024)—a 46% drop in a single year. EY notes the Council is approaching reserve exhaustion and flags going concern as a high inherent risk. They state it is "likely" they will need to consider qualification of their going concern opinion.
findings.matters: Reserve depletion at this pace leaves no buffer for shocks or service interruptions. Going concern qualification would signal insolvency risk.
findings.figures: £81.1m to £43.2m in one year; £6m overspend in 2022/23, £8.5m in 2023/24
findings.quote: The Council exceeded budget by £6m in 2022/23 and £8.5m in 2023/24 with general fund balances reducing from £81.1m at the 31 March 2023 to £43.2m at the 31 March 2024.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Provisional Audit Planning Report (Update) of Ernst & Young LLP - 2024/25 , item 35.
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127421/Appendix A for Provisional Audit Planning Report Update of Ernst Young LLP - 202425.pdf
findings.headline: Consecutive disclaimed audit opinions: 2023/24 disclaimed, 2024/25 expected to be disclaimed again
findings.detail: Because EY could not gain assurance over 2023/24 closing balances, they cannot assure the 2024/25 opening balances. Without prior-year assurance and without rebuilding work (pending system leader guidance), EY will not have sufficient evidence for closing balances and expects to issue another disclaimed opinion. This means the financial statements are unreliable for two consecutive years.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance directors cannot trust the reported financial position. Disclaimed opinions are exceptional; two years running signals a council in serious difficulty.
findings.figures: 2023/24 draft, 2024/25 forecast
findings.quote: we will not be able to obtain sufficient evidence to have reasonable assurance over all closing balances. We therefore expect to again issue a disclaimed audit opinion in 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: Government cancellation of HS2 Phase 2 forced £8.7m immediate write-off against reserves with no recovery prospect
findings.detail: Council had expected future HS2 funding to cover project costs. Government cancellation forced costs to be treated as immediate revenue expense and written off against reserves, causing unexpected depletion of already-low reserves.
findings.matters: Unexpected government decision forced material hit to depleted reserves; demonstrates council's exposure to major decisions beyond its control
findings.figures: £8.7m HS2 revenue write-off in 2024/25
findings.quote: The Government's decision to cancel HS2 Phase 2 also meant that costs associated with that project, that were expected to be funded from future income, were expected to be funded from existing reserves, with no prospect of future income.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: 2025/26 shows £25.3m budget gap despite £53m of savings proposals; 2026/27 has £21.6m gap
findings.detail: Council identified £70m of budget pressures in 2025/26. After £53m of savings proposals and 4.99% Council Tax increase, a £25.3m gap remained and was covered by additional EFS. Structural deficit continues into 2026/27 with £21.6m gap.
findings.matters: Budget problem not being resolved despite significant savings efforts; structural deficit persists year-on-year suggesting systemic pressures exceed council's management capacity
findings.figures: £70m pressures identified 2025/26; £53m savings proposals; £25.3m gap 2025/26; £21.6m gap 2026/27
findings.quote: The Council identified updated pressures totalling over £70m

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: 2024/25 overspend of £17.6m consumed entire approved Exceptional Financial Support, leaving no contingency
findings.detail: Despite monthly reviews by Strategic Finance Management Board, spending still exceeded budget by £17.6m. Entire EFS allocation had to be used just to maintain solvency, with no buffer remaining.
findings.matters: Demonstrates inability to control spending within budget even with active oversight; emergency funding fully committed with no contingency for further pressures
findings.figures: £17.6m overspend 2024/25 against budget of £387.4m
findings.quote: The out-turn position, net of proposed transfers to useable reserves of £7.6m, was an overspend of £17.6m. This was funded by the application of the full amount of approved Exceptional Financial Support.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: Finance director formally stated dissatisfaction with reserve strategy adequacy in February 2024 budget
findings.detail: S151 Officer assessed that reserves strategy does not present adequate level to support medium-term financial strategy. This formal assessment signals governance concern and lack of officer confidence in financial viability.
findings.matters: Chief finance officer's formal assessment that financial strategy is inadequate is material governance risk signal for potential lenders
findings.figures: S151 assessment recorded in 2024/25 budget approval February 2024
findings.quote: the S151 was not satisfied that the Reserves Strategy presented an adequate level of reserves to support the MTFS

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: Council carries £284m accumulated debt; interest rate rises already identified as 'material problem' for debt servicing
findings.detail: Debt accumulated from infrastructure projects, budget overruns, and unfunded SEND education deficits. Interest rate rises in 2022–23 already made servicing unaffordable. Interest and MRP costs grew by £9.5m in 2024/25 budget.
findings.matters: Large debt burden with interest already unaffordable; further rate rises could severely constrain budget flexibility or force asset sales
findings.figures: £284m total accumulated debt; £9.5m interest and MRP costs in 2024/25 budget growth
findings.quote: Repayment of interest on these debts became a material problem following the rapid rise in interest rates in 2022 and 2023.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: Council has received emergency government funding three years running; states it will continue to need it to balance budgets
findings.detail: DLUHC approved £17.6m Exceptional Financial Support for 2023/24–2024/25, with additional EFS for 2025/26. Council explicitly states it will 'continue to be reliant on either further EFS or a significant improvement in the level of grant' to balance future years.
findings.matters: Structural budget that cannot balance without government bailout; lenders face exposure if government withdraws or reduces emergency support
findings.figures: £17.6m EFS 2023/24–2024/25; additional EFS approved for 2025/26
findings.quote: In February 2024, DLUHC provisionally agreed EFS for 2023/24 and 2024/25 totalling £17.6m

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: General reserves depleted to £5.6m; finance director warns 1% budget variance would trigger Section 114 insolvency notice
findings.detail: 2023/24 deficit reduced general reserves from £12.6m to £5.6m (1.6% of budget). Council states this position is 'clearly unsustainable' because a 1% spending variance (approximately £3.9m) would trigger statutory insolvency. Almost no buffer remains for unexpected costs.
findings.matters: Section 114 notice means loss of financial autonomy and forced statutory intervention; council has eliminated its financial buffer and faces existential risk from any adverse variance
findings.figures: General reserves £5.6m at 2023/24 outturn (1.6% of £353.1m net revenue budget)
findings.quote: This position being clearly unsustainable as a 1% variance in spending could trigger the requirement for a Section 114 report.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Statement of Accounts Update 2324 , item 32.
findings.headline: High Needs education deficit identified as single greatest financial risk, now £112m
findings.detail: The DSG accumulated deficit grew from £78.6m at March 2024 to £112m at March 2025—a £33.4m increase in one year. The council has flagged this as its single greatest financial risk for several years. This represents a structural unfunded pressure that will persist indefinitely.
findings.matters: Largest single constraint on council finances; any lender assessing credit risk must evaluate whether the council can manage this ongoing drain
findings.figures: Accumulated deficit £78.6m at 31 March 2024; £112m at 31 March 2025; in-year deficit £51.3m in 2024/25
findings.quote: The single greatest financial risk to the Council remains the substantial and growing deficit on High Needs spending from the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG).

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Final Annual Governance Statement 2023/24 , item 33.
findings.headline: External audit completion pending on 2023/24 accounts due to unresolved objection
findings.detail: The draft Statement of Accounts 2023/24 was reported to Audit and Governance Committee on 29 July 2024. External Auditors will provide an interim report pending completion of their work on 'the objection to the 2023/24 accounts' at the February 2025 committee meeting. An objection to the accounts indicates a third party has formally challenged the accounts, delaying final audit sign-off.
findings.matters: Unresolved objection to accounts delays final audit sign-off and formal accountability; signals potential material disputes over financial position or transactions.
findings.figures: Interim audit report expected February 2025
findings.quote: The External Auditors will provide an interim report on the Council's accounts for 2023/24 to the Audit and Governance Committee on 24 February 2025 pending the completion of their work on the objection to the 2023/24 accounts.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Final Annual Governance Statement 2023/24 , item 33.
findings.headline: Section 106 planning obligations funds subject to 'No Assurance' audit rating with delays in corrective action implementation
findings.detail: Planning service modernisation workstreams include specific audit of Section 106 funds, which received a 'No Assurance' audit report during 2023/24. Progress made on audit recommendations with 2 recommendations outstanding as of November 2024. Infrastructure Funding Statement published end November. However, addressing issues with legacy agreements is scheduled for Q1 2025/26 - indicating delayed resolution of control failures over planning obligations.
findings.matters: No Assurance rating on material planning obligation funds indicates control environment failure and financial risk; delays in implementing corrective actions demonstrate weak governance response.
findings.figures: 2 audit recommendations outstanding as of November 2024; legacy agreements target completion Q1 2025/26
findings.quote: A significant 'No Assurance' report was also provided during the year in relation to the arrangements of Section 106 funds, which has subsequently had delays in implementing actions within agreed timescales.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Final Annual Governance Statement 2023/24 , item 33.
findings.headline: Section 151 Officer and other key statutory officers departed mid-year with interim replacements
findings.detail: Section 151 Officer left the Council on 6 May 2024; an Interim Director was appointed and arrangements 'continues into 2024/25'. Director of Governance and Compliance (Monitoring Officer) left August 2024; Head of Legal appointed as Acting Director pending permanent appointment. Executive Director for Children's Services left July 2024 with Interim ED joining October 2024. This follows departures of Chief Executive (October 2023) and Executive Director Place (October 2023), though permanent CE took up post January 2024 and permanent Place ED joined December 2024.
findings.matters: Loss of statutory finance and governance officers mid-year with continued interim arrangements signals instability in senior finance and compliance capability; risks inadequate financial controls and audit oversight.
findings.figures: Section 151 Officer departure May 2024; Monitoring Officer departure August 2024; Children's Services ED departure July 2024
findings.quote: In February 2024, it was announced that the Section 151 Officer would be leaving the Council in May 2024. Subsequently, an Interim Section 151 Officer was appointed, and this arrangement continues into 2024/25. In August 2024, the Director of Governance and Compliance (Monitoring Officer) left the Council. The Head of Legal (and Deputy Monitoring Officer) has been appointed as the Acting Director of Governance and Compliance (now Governance, Compliance and Monitoring Officer) to cover this role, pending appointment to the role on a permanent basis.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Final Annual Governance Statement 2023/24 , item 33.
findings.headline: Considering use of capitalisation direction borrowing due to continued financial pressure in 2024/25
findings.detail: The Council received notification of potential Exceptional Financial Support up to £11.6m for 2023/24 and up to £6m for 2024/25, available as capitalisation direction (borrowing). While not required in 2023/24, this is now 'being considered as part of 2024/25' - meaning the council expects to need exceptional government support and is evaluating costly borrowing options to cover deficits.
findings.matters: Reliance on exceptional financial support and costlier capitalisation direction borrowing (at premium interest rates) indicates deteriorating financial position and increased long-term debt servicing burden.
findings.figures: Up to £11.6m for 2023/24 items; up to £6m for 2024/25; costs incurred 'in the form of premium interest rates and additional borrowing costs'
findings.quote: The Council received notification from Government of the potential to utilise 'Exceptional Financial Support' – of up to £11.6m relating to 2023/24 items, and up to £6m in respect of 2024/25 – but as expected this is only in the form of capitalisation direction (which will cost us to deploy, in the form of premium interest rates and additional borrowing costs). This was not required in 2023/24 but is being considered as part of 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Final Annual Governance Statement 2023/24 , item 33.
findings.headline: Council must reduce spending by £100 million over four years to achieve financial sustainability
findings.detail: The Council faces ongoing financial pressures with declining reserves and use of one-off funding sources to balance budgets. The 2023/24 outturn showed an overspend that was only slightly smaller than forecast, and smaller overspends 'did not alleviate the pressure in future years' because one-off funding sources used will no longer be available. A transformation programme with a target of £100m spending reduction over four years has been commissioned.
findings.matters: A required 25% spending reduction over four years signals fundamental structural deficit and execution risk; the council is dependent on transformation success to remain solvent.
findings.figures: £100 million reduction required over four years
findings.quote: Our plan needs to present a version of Cheshire East Council that spends £100m less over the next four years.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Final Annual Governance Statement 2023/24 , item 33.
findings.headline: Internal audit opinion on control framework downgraded to 'Limited' for first time since 2009
findings.detail: The Council's Internal Audit opinion assessed the framework of risk management, control and governance as 'Limited' for 2023/24 - the first limitation in 15 years. This reflects significant findings where controls either failed to be applied or were absent entirely. A major 'No Assurance' report was issued on Section 106 funds arrangements, with subsequent delays in implementing corrective actions.
findings.matters: A limited audit opinion signals material control weaknesses across the organisation that increase financial and reputational risk and suggest the council cannot reliably execute its statutory duties.
findings.figures: First limitation since 2009; 'No Assurance' report on Section 106 funds
findings.quote: The Head of Audit and Risk Management's opinion as the Chief Audit Executive on the Council's framework for governance, risk management and internal control for 2023/24 has been given as 'limited'. This is the first time since 2009 that there has been a limitation on this opinion.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Self Assessment , item 37.
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127496/Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Self Assessment.pdf
findings.headline: Audit committee has combined responsibility for Standards matters with its core audit function
findings.detail: Question 1 is marked as only partly meeting good practice: the committee has taken on responsibility for Standards matters in addition to its core audit and governance functions. CIPFA guidance recommends dedicated audit committees to maintain focus.
findings.matters: Dilution of audit committee focus between audit oversight and standards/ethics functions can reduce the depth of financial control scrutiny that lenders rely on.
findings.figures: Question 1 assessment: Partly (not Yes)
findings.quote: Committee has responsibility for Standards matters in addition to his core functions

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Self Assessment , item 37.
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s127496/Appendix 1 for Audit and Governance Committee Self Assessment.pdf
findings.headline: Council commissioned external CIPFA review of audit committee effectiveness, with action plan implementation underway
findings.detail: The council's Audit and Governance Committee underwent an external CIPFA effectiveness review, after which terms of reference were updated based on CIPFA model guidance and an action plan was implemented. This indicates the external review identified gaps against good practice standards that required remediation.
findings.matters: The need for external review suggests the committee had previously identified deficiencies in meeting governance standards. A lender would want to monitor whether remediation actions are delivered and effective.

findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means a lender cannot rely on independently-verified accounts to assess the council's financial position, creating uncertainty about loan covenant compliance and financial health.

findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s126438/Draft Statement and Outturn Report 2024-25 - Cheshire East v3.pdf
findings.headline: Capital programme slippage reached 39%, significantly higher than the prior year's 18%, while the council plans substantial borrowing for future capital investment
findings.detail: Expenditure on the capital programme was £88.4m against a revised budget of £144.7m, leaving £56.3m slipped into future years. findings.matters: High capital slippage suggests poor project delivery or budget planning; heavy reliance on borrowing for capital means increasing debt servicing costs that will pressure future revenue budgets—especially concerning given the council already cannot balance its current budget.

findings.detail: The closing balance on the General Fund Balance is £6.3m. Against a revised budget of £365.8m, this represents only 1.7% of annual spending—well below typical minimum reserves of 3-5% and leaving minimal buffer for unexpected pressures.

findings.detail: Cheshire East overspent its revenue budget by £17.6m (4.8%) against a revised budget of £365.8m. findings.matters: Indicates the council cannot manage spending within its budget and must resort to exceptional government support to balance its finances—a red flag for any lender considering credit risk.

findings.figures: Deadline was 30 June 2025, 75% of councils met this nationally
findings.quote: The statutory deadline for the publication of the draft accounts was 30 June 2025. The Council has been unable to meet this requirement due to: Significant additional statutory requirements associated with implementing new accounting standard IFR16 – Leases and associated lease valuations, Delays in obtaining accurate fixed asset valuations and resourcing challenges experienced in 2024-25.

findings.paper_title: Audit and Governance Supplementary Agenda - Item 8 Draft Pre-audited Statement of Accounts 2024/25 and Outturn Update 2024/25
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/b28726/Audit and Governance Supplementary Agenda - Item 8 Draft Pre-audited Statement of Accounts 202425 a.pdf?T=9
findings.headline: 39% capital programme slippage, worsening from prior year 18%
findings.detail: Capital spending was £88.4m against a revised budget of £144.7m (39% underspend). This is significantly higher slippage than 2023/24's 18%. The council carried out a capital review to reduce borrowing-funded spending, which led to this substantial slippage.
findings.matters: Rising slippage suggests delivery risk or reprioritisation of schemes. Combined with high borrowing in the capital programme, it indicates the council may struggle to execute its capital plan.
findings.figures: £88.4m actual, £144.7m budget, £56.3m slippage, 39% variance vs 18% prior year
findings.quote: Expenditure on the capital programme is £ 88.4m against a revised budget of £ 144.7m that was reported to the Finance Sub Committee in January 2025. The underspend of £56.3 will be slipped into 2025/26 and future years. This level of slippage, at 39%, is a higher variance than 2023/24 (18%).

findings.paper_title: Audit and Governance Supplementary Agenda - Item 8 Draft Pre-audited Statement of Accounts 2024/25 and Outturn Update 2024/25
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/b28726/Audit and Governance Supplementary Agenda - Item 8 Draft Pre-audited Statement of Accounts 202425 a.pdf?T=9
findings.headline: £17.6m revenue overspend funded by emergency capitalisation direction borrowing
findings.detail: The council overran its revised budget of £365.8m by £17.6m (4.8% overspend), closing General Fund reserves at only £6.3m. This overspend was funded via Exceptional Financial Support using a Capitalisation Direction, which allows borrowing to cover revenue spending rather than capital investment.
findings.matters: Emergency borrowing to cover operational overspend indicates structural budget problems and reduces the council's financial flexibility. Low reserves leave minimal buffer for future pressures.
findings.figures: £17.6m overspend, £365.8m revised budget, £6.3m General Fund closing balance
findings.quote: A Net Revenue Overspend of £ 17.6m against a revised budget of £ 365.8m (4.8% variance) funded by (£17.6m) conditional Exceptional Financial Support (Capitalisation Direction) via borrowing.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Internal Audit Opinion 2024-25 , item 20.
findings.headline: Critical strategic risks have persisted for considerable periods alongside vacancies and interim arrangements in leadership.
findings.detail: The Strategic Risk Register shows multiple critically-rated risks that have been present for considerable periods. The council simultaneously faces 'continued vacancies and interim arrangements across the executive and wider leadership structure' and 'wider issues within the Planning service'. These combine to create execution risk in stabilizing the organisation.
findings.matters: Long-standing critical risks combined with leadership gaps and interim arrangements indicate the council lacks stable management capacity to resolve fundamental operational issues.
findings.figures: Multiple critically-rated risks present for considerable periods; interim/vacant executive positions
findings.quote: The consistent reporting on the Council's Strategic Risk Register during the year, has highlighted a number of critically rated risks which have been present for considerable periods of time.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Internal Audit Opinion 2024-25 , item 20.
findings.headline: Council applied for Exceptional Financial Support from government in 2023/24 and 2024/25.
findings.detail: The Council sought Exceptional Financial Support from the Secretary of State for Levelling Up to support reserve levels returning to approximately 5% of the net revenue budget. This indicates the council cannot maintain minimum reserves from operating cash flow and is dependent on government intervention.
findings.matters: Reliance on government emergency support to maintain minimum reserves signals financial stress and reduced financial resilience to absorb service pressures or unexpected costs.
findings.figures: Reserves at approximately 5% of net revenue budget, maintained only through Exceptional Financial Support
findings.quote: The Council's application to the Secretary of State for Levelling Up for Exceptional Financial Support in 2023/24 and 2024/25 to support reserve levels returning to approximately 5% of the net revenue budget.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Internal Audit Opinion 2024-25 , item 20.
findings.headline: External auditors have disclaimed opinion on 2023/24 accounts; 2024/25 accounts will also be disclaimed.
findings.detail: Ernst & Young's late appointment limited audit scope on 2023/24. Objections to the accounts were received and external audit was not completed. The external auditors issued a disclaimed opinion for 2023/24 accounts. Due to lack of assurance on opening balances, the 2024/25 financial statements will also receive a disclaimed opinion.
findings.matters: A lender cannot verify the council's financial position or asset values for two consecutive years, creating fundamental uncertainty about the reliability of financial data for covenant purposes.
findings.figures: Two consecutive years with disclaimed audit opinions: 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.quote: This resulted in the external auditors providing a disclaimed audit opinion for the 2023/24 accounts and a failure to meet the backstop date for publication. As a result of this and the lack of assurance in relation to the opening balances, the 2024/25 financial statements will also be disclaimed.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Internal Audit Opinion 2024-25 , item 20.
findings.headline: Internal control framework rated 'Limited' with a concerning breakdown of controls across audited areas.
findings.detail: The Chief Audit Executive's opinion on internal control is 'Limited'. Of 80 audit recommendations raised in 21 reports, 31% relate to failure to apply existing controls, 36% to control design weaknesses, and 9% to absence of expected controls. The audit concludes this demonstrates 'a concerning breakdown of the control environment in the areas subject to review.'
findings.matters: Weak controls in a local authority create elevated fraud and error risk, undermining the reliability of financial reporting and the council's ability to safeguard assets.
findings.figures: 31% failure to apply controls; 36% design weaknesses; 9% absent controls; 80 recommendations across 21 reports
findings.quote: This demonstrates a concerning breakdown of the control environment in the areas subject to review.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Draft Financial Statements – Wholly Owned Companies 2024/25 and Outturn Update 2024/25 , item 18.
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s126212/Appendix A for Draft Financial Statements Wholly Owned Companies 202425 and Outturn Update 20242.pdf
findings.headline: Council extracted £1.5m interim dividends from subsidiaries whilst reserves were falling £1.116m
findings.detail: The council paid itself £1.5m in interim dividends from the wholly owned companies during 2024/25 in the same period when those companies' combined reserves fell by £1.116m, representing cash extraction that exceeds the reserve decline.
findings.matters: Dividend extraction during reserve depletion indicates either strong operational cash generation offsetting balance-sheet decline, or financial stress—either scenario warrants scrutiny by a lender or finance director.
findings.figures: £1.5m interim dividends paid; £1.116m reserve decrease
findings.quote: Interim Dividends were paid by the companies to CEC in 24/25 to the value of £1.5m.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A for Draft Financial Statements – Wholly Owned Companies 2024/25 and Outturn Update 2024/25 , item 18.
findings.paper_url: https://moderngov.cheshireeast.gov.uk/ecminutes/documents/s126212/Appendix A for Draft Financial Statements Wholly Owned Companies 202425 and Outturn Update 20242.pdf
findings.headline: Wholly owned company reserves fell £1.116m in 2024/25, accelerating six-fold from prior year's £0.173m decline
findings.detail: Combined reserves of the wholly owned companies decreased by £1.116m in 2024/25, up sharply from the prior year's £0.173m decrease. This accelerating depletion has reduced retained reserves to only £0.848m, equivalent to less than 2% of the £43.611m net spending by these entities.
findings.matters: Rapidly depleting reserves in council-controlled subsidiaries reduce the financial buffer against operational challenges or cost shocks in critical services including waste management and bereavement services.
findings.figures: £1.116m decrease (2023/24 £0.173m), retained reserves £0.848m, net spending £43.611m
findings.quote: WOC Reserves decreased by £1.116m (2023/24 £0.173m), leaving retained reserves at £0.848m.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024-25 , item 22.
findings.headline: Dependency on Exceptional Financial Support with uncertain path to sustainable finances post-2026
findings.detail: The council used exceptional financial support to set balanced budgets in both February 2024 and February 2025. The statement explicitly notes the need to develop a sustainable Medium Term Financial Strategy post-EFS as the council progresses through 2025-26, indicating current spending is not sustainable on normal resources alone.
findings.matters: Reliance on exceptional support signals structural budget imbalance. Uncertainty about post-support sustainability creates medium-term financial risk and reduces borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: EFS provided for both 2024-25 and 2025-26; need for new sustainable MTFS post-EFS
findings.quote: As we progress through 2025/26, it is important that steps are taken to develop a sustainable MTFS post EFS to ensure the ongoing financial sustainability of the Council.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024-25 , item 22.
findings.headline: Audit opinion limited for first time since 2009, with Section 106 funds control failure and delayed remediation
findings.detail: The 2023-24 internal audit opinion was limited, the first time since 2009. Findings showed existing controls were not applied or expected controls were absent across the council. A significant 'No Assurance' report was issued on Section 106 funds management, with subsequent delays in implementing corrective actions. While 2024-25 shows no new 'No Assurance' reports, the prior control failures and delayed fixes remain concerning.
findings.matters: Limited audit opinion is a material control red flag. Section 106 funds (developer contributions) mismanagement creates legal risk and may affect future planning authority standing and developer confidence.
findings.figures: Limited audit opinion; first since 2009; 'No Assurance' report on Section 106 funds with delayed implementation of fixes
findings.quote: This was also demonstrated by the Head of Audit, Risk & Assurance's opinion as the Chief Audit Executive on the Council's framework for governance, risk management and internal control for 2023/24 being given as 'limited'. This is the first time since 2009 that there has been a limitation on this opinion. A significant 'No Assurance' report was also provided during the year in relation to the arrangements of Section 106 funds.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024-25 , item 22.
findings.headline: Cheshire and Merseyside ICB in financial turnaround with £170m required savings, creating risk of cost-shifting to council
findings.detail: The Integrated Care Board that provides health partnership to the council is formally in financial turnaround and must make £170m in cashable savings. Since ICB spending is mostly on NHS hospitals and staffing, savings pressure falls on jointly funded services including Continuing Health Care and services for vulnerable adults and children, creating risk the NHS will reduce expenditure expecting the council to absorb costs.
findings.matters: If the NHS reduces funding for jointly-provided services, the council will face additional and potentially unfunded costs for vulnerable populations, directly worsening budget sustainability.
findings.figures: £170m required ICB savings; Cheshire and Merseyside ICB described as one of most financially challenged in country
findings.quote: Cheshire and Merseyside ICB is one of the most financially challenged ICBs in the country and is formally in financial turnaround and required to make cashable savings of approximately £170 million. The key risk is that the NHS will seek to reduce its expenditure in the expectation that the local authority will meet costs of services to vulnerable adults and children to prevent harm.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Draft Annual Governance Statement 2024-25 , item 22.
